evals.prompt: This Roblox project has InputBegan checks in Combat.client.lua, a separate MobileFireButton script, and a controller script that fires a different remote. Make the whole game work on keyboard/mouse, phones/tablets, gamepad/TV, and VR without rewriting standard character movement. I want complete code and a test report, not just advice.
evals.expected_output: A project-specific migration that inventories current inputs, creates semantic actions and contexts, routes all device bindings through one controller path, preserves default movement/camera, centralizes prompts/device switching, fixes server authority, and reports emulated versus physical test status.
assertions: The output identifies and removes or adapts duplicate device-specific mechanic paths rather than preserving separate fire logic.
The output provides an action/context map covering keyboard/mouse, touch, gamepad, and VR or documents justified exclusions.
The implementation uses semantic InputActions/controllers rather than scattering new hardware key checks.
The output preserves Roblox default character movement/camera unless it gives a mechanic-specific reason to replace them.
The remote contract sends intent and keeps damage/cooldown/ammo validation on the server.
The final test report distinguishes Studio emulation from physical-device testing and lists untested hardware honestly.

evals.prompt: My shop works with a mouse, but on Xbox the selection disappears after I buy an item, Button B sometimes closes the whole shop instead of the confirmation dialog, and the list won't scroll to the selected card. Fix the controller and TV experience and keep mouse/touch working.
evals.expected_output: A focused UI-navigation repair with a modal/focus stack, deterministic entry/restoration, explicit links where needed, selected-item scrolling, top-modal cancel behavior, visible TV-scale focus states, Activated-based buttons, and pointer/touch coexistence.
assertions: The solution treats the confirmation dialog as the top modal and makes cancel close one level only.
The solution restores a valid prior selection after purchase or modal close and handles removed/disabled items.
The selected card is scrolled into view rather than merely assigning GuiService.SelectedObject.
Ordinary button activation uses GuiButton.Activated or an equivalent cross-input semantic path.
The solution includes a visible selected state and large-display readability/safe-margin checks.
Mouse and touch paths remain usable and gamepad focus is restored when PreferredInput returns to gamepad.

evals.prompt: Design and implement mobile controls for a third-person Roblox shooter. Players must move, drag the camera, hold aim, fire, reload, swap weapons, and interact at the same time on small phones and tablets. The PC/controller versions already exist.
evals.expected_output: A touch control design and implementation integrated into the existing semantic actions, with thumb zones, safe areas, multi-touch ownership, camera gestures, button sizing, aim assistance, device/orientation adaptation, and hardware testing cases.
assertions: Touch controls bind to the same semantic actions and gameplay controllers as PC/controller rather than duplicating combat logic.
The layout reserves movement and camera zones, respects safe insets, and adapts for small phone versus tablet dimensions.
The implementation explicitly handles simultaneous movement, camera, aim/fire, and touch cancellation/ownership.
Required actions do not depend on hover, right-click, or precision drag.
Aim assistance is described as a tunable touch adaptation while server hit/damage authority remains unchanged.
The test plan includes real phone/tablet multi-touch and orientation/aspect-ratio cases, not Studio simulation alone.

evals.prompt: Add Quest-style VR support to my Roblox dungeon game: teleport and smooth movement, snap/smooth turn, grabbing keys and two-handed weapons, melee, wrist inventory, recenter, seated mode, and controller loss recovery. Keep desktop and controller support intact.
evals.expected_output: A VR-specific extension to the shared action architecture using VRService, comfort settings, tracked-pose conversion, validated locomotion/grab/combat contracts, world/wrist UI, lifecycle recovery, and both emulated and physical headset tests.
assertions: VR is detected through VRService and the solution does not use deprecated UserInputService VR pose/detection APIs.
The headset pose is never overridden, smoothed, or rotated as a desktop camera.
Teleport, grab, throw, and melee outcomes are revalidated by the server with range/state/plausibility checks.
Both comfort locomotion/turn choices and seated/recenter behavior are implemented or explicitly scoped.
Two-handed interactions define release and tracking-loss behavior.
The test report separates Quest/Studio emulation from physical headset comfort, tracking, and performance tests.

evals.prompt: Audit our Roblox controls before console launch. We use ContextActionService in some modules, UserInputService in others, hard-coded [E] prompts, custom vehicle sticks, drag-only inventory, and a menu that assumes IsTenFootInterface. Give us a staged patch plan and implement the safe first stage.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-based audit and staged migration that catalogs bindings, flags deprecated and inaccessible patterns, defines the semantic target architecture, implements a reversible first stage, and supplies validation/test gates.
assertions: The audit finds direct key coupling, spawn/static prompts, drag-only UI, mixed input stacks, and deprecated ten-foot detection.
The plan names one binding owner per semantic action and avoids double-binding IAS and CAS during migration.
TV presentation is based on current input/display/layout signals rather than platform identity inferred from IsTenFootInterface.
The first stage is reversible and includes a concrete action inventory/router or adapter rather than a wholesale untested rewrite.
Vehicle analog values are preserved and deadzone/curve ownership is documented.
Release gates include no-pointer UI completion, controller disconnect/hot-swap, and physical controller/TV testing.

evals.prompt: We have a build mode with a mouse gizmo, keyboard shortcuts, touch drag handles, and no gamepad path. Convert it to work everywhere. The grid has 60 objects, items stream in/out, users can rename builds, and placement must stay server-secure.
evals.expected_output: A scalable cross-device build/editor design with semantic placement actions, pointer/touch adapters, gamepad ray or virtual cursor plus snapping, VR interaction if in scope, virtualized focus-safe UI, text-entry contexts, and server validation.
assertions: The solution provides non-pointer gamepad controls for placement, rotation, depth/mode changes, undo/redo, and property panels.
Pointer/touch drag remains an adapter to shared semantic operations rather than a separate authoritative placement system.
TextBox focus enters a text-entry context and prevents build/gameplay shortcuts while typing or using IME/on-screen keyboard.
Dynamic/streamed item removal cannot leave focus or interaction targeting on a destroyed object.
The server validates placement bounds, permissions, collision/rules, cost, and rate rather than accepting client CFrames as truth.
The test plan covers long/virtualized grids, hot-swap, streamed removal, multiple aspect ratios, and network latency.
